tests.notes: && does not evaluate the right operand when the left is false, so its side effect does not happen; a converter lowering && to a bitwise AND of both sides gets this wrong
|| does not evaluate the right operand when the left is true, so its side effect does not happen
b != 0 && a / b > 1 must not panic with 0x12 when b is zero, because the division is never evaluated
i < items.length && items[i] == x must not panic with 0x32 when i is out of range, because the read is never evaluated
operands of && and || run strictly left to right and stop as soon as the result is known; trace records the call order (runAnd == 123, runOr == 31, runAndStops == 3)
&& has higher precedence than ||: a || b && c means a || (b && c); differs from (a || b) && c for a=true, b=false, c=false
!!a == a and De Morgan's laws hold for every input
comparison results are bool and combine directly with &&, || and !
logical expressions as conditions in if, while and require; requireEither(false, false) reverts with "neither"
logical results stored into a bool state variable, including toggling with !
nested and mixed logical expressions exercise control-flow lowering of several short-circuit operators in one expression
!(a == b) agrees with a != b and !(a < b) agrees with a >= b for every input
&& requires bool operands; integers have no truthiness and are not implicitly converted
! requires a bool operand; test an integer for zero with x == 0
mixing a bool with an integer variable in || is rejected; the integer is not converted to bool
conditions must be bool; there is no non-zero-is-true rule
the integer literal 1 is not the bool true and is not accepted as an operand of &&
an integer cannot be assigned to a bool variable, not even the literals 0 and 1
there is no ^^ operator; on bool, a != b gives logical XOR (see comparison/008)
